alternatives.reason: The consumer manifest is a governed source document; mutating it from the control plane would destroy provenance and the immutable-version guarantee.
Owner decision 2026-09-20: JSON files first behind a Store interface; Firestore only if Week 3 has slack.
Architecture §Environment lifecycle: no hard delete for referenced environments; retire keeps history readable.

architecture_impact: Adds internal/topology: EnvironmentTopology versions are immutable snapshots chained by previous_version with a config_hash; version 1 is bootstrapped from project.yaml and labelled origin=manifest.
Add, edit, reorder, retire and restore each create a new version and an append-only audit event; every mutation carries expected_version and is refused with 409 when stale.

Material changes (type, sequence, target_ref, required_evidence, approver_policy, status) publish STALE invalidations for the Project's observed decisions with a visible reason; display_name and owner are informational.
Production may be renamed for display but its standard type cannot change and it cannot be retired (PRODUCTION_PROTECTED); it carries READ_ONLY_BLOCKED_IN_P0.
The registry API stays read-only and keeps reporting manifest environments; the topology is a separate governance surface under /v1/projects/{id}/environments.
The React workspace gains an Environment Topology panel and overlays STALE on invalidated decisions; header now distinguishes REGISTRY READ-ONLY from TOPOLOGY VERSIONED.
cost_assumptions: No cloud resources; JSON files under CONTEXT_RAIL_STATE_DIR (instance-local /tmp on Cloud Run, not durable).
unknowns: Durable persistence target (GCS vs Firestore) and the migration of existing JSON state.
Actor identity: X-ContextRail-Actor is recorded, not authenticated; real membership/authorization is a later slice.

Which decisions depend on which environment: P0 invalidates every observed decision of the Project on a material change; a per-decision environment binding needs the DecisionRecord contract from VS-004.
acceptance_criteria: UI-05: add, edit, reorder, retire, restore each produce a new topology version visible in the workspace.
Material edits mark observed decisions STALE with a visible reason; display-only edits do not.
Retired environments keep their history and cannot be edited until restored; production cannot be retired or re-typed.
A stale expected_version is refused with 409 and the operator is told to reload.
Consumer fixture trees are byte-identical before and after the full browser journey.

human_decision.reason: Owner instructed to continue immediately after the Cloud Run baseline; VS-003 is the second half of the 2026-09-27 checkpoint. JSON-file persistence was the owner's explicit choice. Accepts local development/testing only; no deployment authorization.
